learningObjectives.text: Explain this episode: What does the embassy offer Achilles?
Use the cited passage to explain: Why is the embassy more than a payment negotiation?

main.author: Homer
main.locator: Book 9, Achilles answers the embassy; Book 9, normalized characters 15931-16232
main.excerpt: purpose that there be no more of this cajoling, from whatsoever quarter it may come. Him do I hate even as the gates of hell who says one thing while he hides another in his heart; therefore I will say what I mean. I will be appeased neither by Agamemnon son of Atreus nor by any other of the Danaans,
main.note: Verbatim local text with whitespace normalized. Lesson analysis is interpretation, not part of this quotation.

narrativeBlocks.title: The scene
narrativeBlocks.body: Odysseus, Phoenix, and Ajax visit Achilles with an offer of gifts. Achilles does not accept a return on those terms: compensation has not settled the injury to his standing or his doubts about fighting.

narrativeBlocks.title: What the source does
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (translation; whitespace normalized): “purpose that there be no more of this cajoling, from whatsoever quarter it may come. Him do I hate even as the gates of hell who says one thing while he hides another in his heart; therefore I will say what I mean. I will be appeased neither by Agamemnon son of Atreus nor by any other of the Danaans,”

narrativeBlocks.title: Why it matters
narrativeBlocks.body: Interpretation: Achilles’ refusal is emotionally intelligible and strategically disastrous; the poem makes both things true at once.

narrativeBlocks.title: Read it carefully
narrativeBlocks.body: Distinguish an offer from a reconciliation. Book 9 lets Achilles question the rewards of fighting; do not reduce his refusal to bargaining for a higher price.

narrativeBlocks.title: Carry it forward
narrativeBlocks.body: This tests whether a hero can be wronged and destructive at the same time.

quiz.prompt: What does the embassy offer Achilles?

choices.text: A command to leave Troy without his men
The kingship of Troy after Hector’s surrender
Gifts and restored standing if he returns to battle

quiz.explanation: Gifts and restored standing if he returns to battle. Revisit the named passage and distinguish its narrative from the lesson’s interpretation.

quiz.prompt: Why is the embassy more than a payment negotiation?

choices.text: Achilles questions honour, trust, and the value of risking his life.
Achilles does not understand what the gifts are worth.
The visitors have come without Agamemnon’s permission.
